Context: in the live final every supplier thread has a 60 s clock from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread. A wave lasts 8 minutes, up to 10 messages per thread. Our runner (buyer/runner.py play_case) sends ONE message at a time per case, round-robin over threads (oldest reply first), and finished threads get a keepalive after 35 s. Each move may call an LLM with a 20 s timeout (buyer/llm.py) plus the arena call latency.

Measure from evidence:
1. logs/runs/*.json (our notes with timestamps `t`), logs/sessions/** (pulled sessions with traces) and exports/ (see exports/README.md): per session, number of supplier threads, per-move gap between supplier reply and our next message, count of timeouts / 409 errors / "missed" moves, total session duration. Focus on the newest runs (by mtime) since the code changed recently.
2. Any log lines "writer paragraph in X s" or "writer model failed" (search logs/ and any *.log): distribution of LLM latency.
3. Compute worst case: with N suppliers (N=2..6) and per-move latency L (arena call ~? s from the data + LLM up to 20 s), does any thread wait >60 s? How many rounds fit in 8 minutes minus the 90 s close margin (deadline_near margin in policy.py)?

Report under 350 words with numbers and file references: observed latencies, timeouts seen, and the N above which the single-threaded loop risks timeouts or runs out of wave time.

Steffen Grabert, steffen.grabert@tum.de

TUM student. Python for data, ML and finance; TypeScript for web and
desktop. Recurring domains: investing and portfolio modelling, football
analytics, study tools.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/agent.py` | which agent plays a case; our strategy grows here |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored) |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

"""The model writes one paragraph of each e-mail: it answers the supplier's last e-mail like a
person would (its questions, its points, its situation). Code writes everything that binds or is
checked: figures, data IDs, the proposal. A paragraph with any digit, data ID or leak is dropped
and the template stands in. Hard timeout: the move goes out without the model if it is late."""

import logging
import os
import re
import time

import httpx

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
TIMEOUT_S = 20.0
FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"\d|\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):|urgent|urgency|deadline|budget|no alternative|"
    r"walk away|other options|last chance|desperate|must close|time pressure|target price",
    re.I,
)

SYSTEM = """You are a senior buyer at Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump maker, writing to a supplier.
Write ONLY the middle paragraph of our reply e-mail: 2 to 4 sentences, plain text, no greeting, no
sign-off, no lists.

In it:
- answer the supplier's last e-mail like a thoughtful person: respond to what it asked and to the
  reasons it gave, using only the facts listed under WHAT WE CAN SAY;
- acknowledge its situation where the notes give one (for example cash needs, full capacity, rising
  costs, a long relationship), sincerely and briefly;
- if it asks for something we cannot give, say so kindly and point to what we do offer;
- ask one short question only if QUESTION ALLOWED is yes.

Never write any number, price, percentage, date, quantity or data ID (code adds the figures). Never
mention urgency, deadlines, a budget, our alternatives or the lack of them, a target price, or that
we will walk away. Never invent facts, promises or commitments. Be polite, factual and warm unless the
tone says firm."""


def complete_from_env():
    """(system, user) -> text with the team's OpenAI-compatible model, or None when not configured."""
    model, key = os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL"), os.environ.get("LLM_API_KEY")
    if not model or not key:
        return None
    base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
    client = httpx.Client(timeout=TIMEOUT_S, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"})

    effort = os.environ.get("LLM_EFFORT", "low")

    def complete(system, user):
        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]
        body = {"model": model, "messages": messages, "reasoning_effort": effort}
        r = client.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

    return complete


def paragraph(complete, brief):
    """The model's paragraph for this brief, or None (no model, late, broken or unsafe)."""
    if complete is None:
        return None
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        text = (complete(SYSTEM, brief) or "").strip()
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a slow or broken model must not cost the move
        log.warning("writer model failed after %.1fs: %s", time.monotonic() - t0, e)
        return None
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    if not text or len(text) > 900 or FORBIDDEN.search(text):
        log.warning("writer paragraph dropped: %r", text[:200])
        return None
    log.info("writer paragraph in %.1fs", time.monotonic() - t0)
    return text

sandbox sessions, joined with the case files and the data package. What we learned from them is
in `docs/learnings.md`. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
(`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better. This is a snapshot: the probe and the script that built
it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.

| File | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
| `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
| `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
| `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |

Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.

`method` in `sessions`:

- `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out
- `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`: an earlier version of the same steps (P01, first P10 run).
- `sandbox A/B: <variant>`: D01 with identical sheets, round 3 varied (`baseline`, `bluff`,
  `urgency`).
- `kit naive agent`: the kit's `NaiveAgent`.

"""The model writes one paragraph of each e-mail: it answers the supplier's last e-mail like a
person would (its questions, its points, its situation). Code writes everything that binds or is
checked: figures, data IDs, the proposal. A paragraph with any digit, data ID or leak is dropped
and the template stands in. Hard timeout: the move goes out without the model if it is late."""

import logging
import os
import re
import time

import httpx

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
TIMEOUT_S = 20.0
FORBIDDEN = re.compile(
    r"\d|\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):|urgent|urgency|deadline|budget|no alternative|"
    r"walk away|other options|last chance|desperate|must close|time pressure|target price",
    re.I,
)

SYSTEM = """You are a senior buyer at Hollerau Pumpenwerke, a German pump maker, writing to a supplier.
Write ONLY the middle paragraph of our reply e-mail: 2 to 4 sentences, plain text, no greeting, no
sign-off, no lists.

In it:
- answer the supplier's last e-mail like a thoughtful person: respond to what it asked and to the
  reasons it gave, using only the facts listed under WHAT WE CAN SAY;
- acknowledge its situation where the notes give one (for example cash needs, full capacity, rising
  costs, a long relationship), sincerely and briefly;
- if it asks for something we cannot give, say so kindly and point to what we do offer;
- ask one short question only if QUESTION ALLOWED is yes.

Never write any number, price, percentage, date, quantity or data ID (code adds the figures). Never
mention urgency, deadlines, a budget, our alternatives or the lack of them, a target price, or that
we will walk away. Never invent facts, promises or commitments. Be polite, factual and warm unless the
tone says firm."""


def complete_from_env():
    """(system, user) -> text with the team's OpenAI-compatible model, or None when not configured."""
    model, key = os.environ.get("LLM_MODEL"), os.environ.get("LLM_API_KEY")
    if not model or not key:
        return None
    base = os.environ.get("LLM_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
    client = httpx.Client(timeout=TIMEOUT_S, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"})

    effort = os.environ.get("LLM_EFFORT", "low")

    def complete(system, user):
        messages = [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]
        body = {"model": model, "messages": messages, "reasoning_effort": effort}
        r = client.post(f"{base}/chat/completions", json=body)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return r.json()["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]

    return complete


def paragraph(complete, brief):
    """The model's paragraph for this brief, or None (no model, late, broken or unsafe)."""
    if complete is None:
        return None
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        text = (complete(SYSTEM, brief) or "").strip()
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - a slow or broken model must not cost the move
        log.warning("writer model failed after %.1fs: %s", time.monotonic() - t0, e)
        return None
    text = " ".join(text.split())
    if not text or len(text) > 900 or FORBIDDEN.search(text):
        log.warning("writer paragraph dropped: %r", text[:200])
        return None
    log.info("writer paragraph in %.1fs", time.monotonic() - t0)
    return text

"""Plays cases with the policy. The arena answers one call per session at a time and each thread's
60-second clock runs from the supplier's reply, so one loop sends one message at a time, always to
the thread whose clock has run longest; finished threads get a short question before their clock
runs out while the others still negotiate; then the cheapest acceptable sheet is accepted.
`play_waves` is the kit's Live Final loop with this runner."""

import functools
import json
import logging
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from arena_kit.client import ArenaError
from arena_kit.play import ENDED, RemoteTable, fetch_documents, latest, moves_left, quota_used_up

from .policy import Negotiator, deadline_near, keepalive_message

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")
RUNS = Path("logs/runs")
KEEPALIVE_AFTER_S = 35  # a finished thread gets a question this long after the supplier's reply


def play_case(table, case_id, pkg=None, deadline=None, complete=None):
    case, threads = table.open(case_id)
    if getattr(table, "done", None):  # resumed a case that had already ended
        return table.done
    for events in threads.values():
        for m in events:
            fetch_documents(table, m)
    neg = Negotiator(case, pkg, complete)
    for sid, events in threads.items():
        neg.setup(sid, events)
    replied = {sid: time.monotonic() for sid in threads}
    # round 1 goes out cheapest quote first: if a clock runs out, it is the least promising one's
    order = sorted(threads, key=lambda sid: neg.sides[sid].quote or float("inf"))
    rank = {sid: i for i, sid in enumerate(order)}
    result = None

    def open_threads():
        return [s for s in threads if neg.sides[s].state not in ("done", "ended") and live(s)]

    def live(sid):
        return latest(threads[sid]).get("status") not in ENDED

    while not deadline_near(deadline):
        todo = sorted(open_threads(), key=lambda s: (replied[s], rank[s]))
        waiting = [
            s
            for s in threads
            if neg.sides[s].state == "done"
            and live(s)
            and todo
            and time.monotonic() - replied[s] > KEEPALIVE_AFTER_S
            and moves_left(case, threads[s]) > 0
        ]
        if not todo:
            break
        if waiting:  # a finished bidder whose clock runs out first: keep it alive
            sid = min(waiting, key=lambda s: replied[s])
            message = keepalive_message(threads[sid])
        else:
            sid = todo[0]
            move = neg.move(sid, threads)
            if move is None:
                continue
            message = move["message"]
        try:
            reply = table.send(sid, message)
        except ArenaError as e:
            if e.status != 409:
                raise
            log.info("%s %s: %s", case_id, sid, e.detail)
            neg.rollback(sid)  # it never got this message: our last offer stands for it
            reply = table.missed(sid, e)
            if "result" in reply:
                result = reply["result"]
                break
            threads[sid].append(reply)
            replied[sid] = time.monotonic()
            continue
        neg.commit(sid)
        threads[sid] += [{**message, "from": "buyer"}, reply]
        replied[sid] = time.monotonic()
    if result is None:
        for events in threads.values():  # the latest quote PDFs: standard terms for the close
            for m in events[-2:]:
                try:
                    fetch_documents(table, m)
                except ArenaError as e:
                    log.warning("%s: document not fetched: %s", case_id, e)
        decision = neg.close(threads)
        try:
            result = table.close(decision["supplier_id"], decision["message"])
        except ArenaError as e:
            log.warning("%s: close failed (%s), accepting a standing sheet", case_id, e)
            result = table.close(*neg.fallback_close(threads))
    save(table.session_id, case_id, neg, result)
    return result


def save(session_id, case_id, neg, result):
    RUNS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    keep = ("deal", "supplier_id", "terms", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "score")
    path = RUNS / f"{case_id.split(':')[-1]}_{session_id}.json"
    out = {"case": case_id, "session": session_id, "notes": neg.notes, "result": {k: result.get(k) for k in keep}}
    path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1, default=str))


def play_all(client, case_ids, pkg=None, parallel=8, complete=None):
    """Practice or sandbox: many cases at once. {case_id: result or the exception that stopped it}."""
    used_up = threading.Event()

    def one(case_id):
        if used_up.is_set():
            return case_id, ArenaError(429, "not started: the practice quota is used up")
        try:
            return case_id, play_case(RemoteTable(client), case_id, pkg, complete=complete)
        except ArenaError as e:
            if quota_used_up(e):
                used_up.set()
            log.warning("%s: %s", case_id, e)
            return case_id, e
        except Exception as e:  # one broken case must not stop the others
            log.exception("%s failed", case_id)
            return case_id, e

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=parallel) as pool:
        return dict(pool.map(one, case_ids))


def play_waves(client, pkg=None, waves=5, parallel=10, poll=5.0, complete=None):
    """The Live Final: wait for each wave, play its cases in parallel within the wave's cap."""
    started, closed, caps = {}, set(), {}

    def one(case, deadline):
        try:
            return play_case(RemoteTable(client, case), case["case_id"], pkg, deadline, complete)
        except Exception as e:  # one broken case must not stop the others

Latency audit of the single-threaded runner (read-only; no arena calls).

**Observed (logs/runs/*.json, 54 runs with timestamps; logs/practice-v1..v6.log)**
- Per-case gap between consecutive sends (one message at a time, so this is LLM + arena call, A+L), single-supplier cases: n=121, median 21.4 s, p90 30.4 s, max 92.4 s (sandbox D01 outlier). Implied arena call A is about 19 s median, about 28 s p90.
- Writer LLM (buyer/llm.py, 20 s timeout): "writer paragraph in" n=73, median 1.8 s, p90 3.4 s, max 6.3 s. "writer model failed": 0. "dropped" (FORBIDDEN regex): 7, template used instead.
- Timeouts: 1 "late" in logs/practice-v5.log (20:06:58, P05 sup:70210, 3-supplier case; rollback followed). Notes contain 1 rollback in total.
- 409s: 2 (practice-v1, P02 "session has ended: no_deal", benign end, not a timeout).
- Threads per session: practice cases mostly 1 supplier; P05 has 3 (practice-v5 and v4 runs); sandbox D02 has 2. Session durations: 1 thread 14 to 120 s; 3 threads 165 to 182 s.
- 3-supplier per-thread gaps between our sends: median about 60 s, 6 of 37 above 80 s. Only one "late" was logged, so the arena's clock likely starts later than our note timestamps. Treat the gaps as an upper bound on the wait.
- Not logged: the supplier reply time, so exact wait-from-reply is inferred.

**Worst case.** Cycle C = L + A. Thread wait from reply to our next send W = (N-1)·C + L_own, must stay under 60 s. The wave budget is 480 s minus 90 s margin = 390 s.

| N | W at median (C=21 s, L=2) | W at p90 (C=32 s) | W if writer hits 20 s timeout at p90 A (C=48) | rounds per thread in 390 s (C=21 / C=32) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 23 s | 34 s | 68 s, breaks | 9.3 / 6.1 |
| 3 | 44 s | 66 s, breaks | breaks | 6.2 / 4.1 |
| 4 | 65 s, breaks | breaks | breaks | 4.6 / 3.0 |
| 5 | 86 s | breaks | breaks | 3.7 / 2.4 |
| 6 | 107 s | breaks | breaks | 3.1 / 2.0 |

The arena allows one call per session at a time, so the loop cannot parallelise within a case. The levers are:
- Cap threads per case at 2 or 3 (drop the least promising quote early).
- Shorten or drop the writer timeout (20 s) on the final.
- Keep per-move bookkeeping small.

**Threshold:** N=2 is safe at median and p90 with a normal writer. N=3 is safe only at median latency and breaks at p90. N>=4 breaks at median latency.

Files: buyer/runner.py (play_case loop, KEEPALIVE_AFTER_S=35), buyer/policy.py (deadline_near margin 90), buyer/llm.py (TIMEOUT_S=20), .venv arena_kit/play.py (MOVE_LIMIT_S=60).
